items.title: [Bug]: gfx1100 (RDNA3): first-call non-determinism + long-seq corruption from Triton paged-attention fallback (ROCm 7.14)
items.body:
> **TL;DR** — On **gfx1100/RDNA3**, vLLM 0.25.1's **Triton paged-attention fallback** is (A) **non-deterministic on the first `generate()` call of a process** (at *any* sequence length — not a long-seq threshold) and (B) **garbled at long context**. The ROCm CK custom paged kernel is gated out because the model's decoder is GQA with **`gqa_ratio=2`** (CK requires `≥3`), forcing the Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d`. A warmup call fixes (A) but not (B); **transformers `sdpa` is deterministic + correct on the same stack**. Full repro (3 scripts + build note + expected outputs): https://gist.github.com/AIwork4me/030fc6a872de36197178c9e8217949d1 ### Your current environment
The output of collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) PyTorch version : 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.14.60850 Python version : 3.12.3 Is CUDA available : True GPU models and configuration : 4x AMD Radeon Pro W7900D (gfx1100, RDNA3) HIP runtime version : 7.14.60850 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.2 [pip3] torch==2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.13.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0 vLLM Version : 0.25.1 (built from source, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1100) ```
Note: vLLM 0.25.1 is **built from source** on ROCm 7.14 (no official gfx1100 wheel at this version), and the hardware is **RDNA3 (gfx1100)**. Reproducing requires gfx1100/RDNA3; **gfx1100 (Radeon Pro W7900) cloud instances** are available from AMD-Radeon GPU providers such as [Radeon Cloud](https://radeon-global.anruicloud.com/) (no affiliation — linked only to lower the hardware barrier, not an endorsement). Build caveat: the implicated `kernel_paged_attention_2d` is a pure-Triton kernel JIT-compiled at runtime, but in this env vLLM's pre-compiled HIP kernels were built against 7.2.1 system headers and run on the 7.14 torch — if a cleanly-7.14-built vLLM does not reproduce, that mismatch is the first thing to rule out (details in the gist README). See the scope question at the end. ### 🐛 Describe the bug On **gfx1100 (RDNA3, Radeon Pro W7900D)**, vLLM 0.25.1 serving a VLM (`tencent/HunyuanOCR`, `HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration`) shows **two distinct problems**, both rooted in the ROCm paged-attention **Triton fallback** that vLLM selects on gfx1100 (the CK custom paged kernel is gated out — see root-cause trail): **Symptom A — first-call non-determinism (not length-gated).** The **first** `generate()` call in a process produces different output from subsequent identical calls. With greedy decoding, three identical (image, prompt) runs give `sha8 = ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` — run 0 (the cold/JIT-compiled first call) diverges, runs 1 & 2 are identical. This reproduces at **both** ~15k vision tokens (2048×1920 page) **and** ~3.8k tokens (1024×960 page) — i.e. it is **not** a long-sequence-threshold effect. A single warmup `generate()` before the measured runs eliminates it: after warmup, three identical runs are byte-identical (`sha8 = fd0cc624, fd0cc624, fd0cc624`). **Symptom B — incorrect (garbled) output at long sequence, even when deterministic.** At full resolution (~15k vision tokens), the warmed/deterministic vLLM output is garbled OCR (`lial Oswuamtntnralglyy Flinamie …`) and does **not** contain the ground-truth text, whereas **transformers** with `attn_implementation="sdpa"` on the **same** ROCm 7.14 / gfx1100 / torch 2.11 stack, on the **same** image, is deterministic **and correct** (GT title present). So the ROCm stack *can* do correct long-sequence bf16 attention for this model; vLLM's path cannot. #### Minimal repro ```python from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams # 2048x1920 page = 15360 ViT patches (long-seq case). Use 1024x960 = 3840 for the short-seq case. W, H = 2048, 1920 im = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), "white"); d = ImageDraw.Draw(im) f = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 96) d.text((120, 120), "Quarterly Financial Summary", font=f, fill="black") im.save("/tmp/page.png") PROMPT = ("提取文档图片中正文的所有信息用markdown格式表示，其中页眉、页脚部分忽略，" "表格用html格式表达，文档中公式用latex格式表示，按照阅读顺序组织进行解析。") llm = LLM(model="tencent/HunyuanOCR", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=32768, gpu_memory_utilization=0.90, enforce_eager=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, trust_remote_code=True) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=-1, max_tokens=1024, repetition_penalty=1.08) prompt = llm.get_tokenizer().apply_chat_template( [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image"}, {"type": "text", "text": PROMPT}]}], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) img = Image.open("/tmp/page.png").convert("RGB") for i in range(3): # Symptom A: run 0 differs from runs 1 & 2 print(i, llm.generate({"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": img}}, sampling_params=sp, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0].text[:80]) ``` Observed (3× identical input, full-res): ```text sha8 = ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624 # run 0 != run 1 == run 2 byte-identical: False GT title present in any run: False # garbled even on the deterministic (warmed) runs ``` #### Evidence summary | experiment (greedy ×3 identical input) | sha8 | deterministic? | correct? | |---|---|---|---| | full-res (15360 tok), no warmup | `ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` | ❌ no (symptom A) | ❌ garbled (symptom B) | | short-seq (3840 tok), no warmup | `f00c87f2, f31888d4, f31888d4` | ❌ no (symptom A is not length-gated) | (image too small to judge) | | full-res (15360 tok), 1 warmup then ×3 | `fd0cc624, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` | ✅ yes (warmup fixes A) | ❌ still garbled (B remains) | | transformers `sdpa`, full-res | `a313e63a ×3` | ✅ yes | ✅ correct | #### Root-cause trail (what I verified) 1. **It is not the vision encoder.** Forcing the ViT/mm-encoder backend to `TORCH_SDPA` (which routes through `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`, via `mm_encoder_attn_backend="TORCH_SDPA"`) changed the output **zero** — byte-identical to the default `FLASH_ATTN` (Triton) ViT path (same sha8s). So the ViT is deterministic in both backends and is not the source. By elimination the divergent path is the **decoder**. 2. **The decoder runs through vLLM's standard paged-attention path.** `HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/hunyuan_vision.py`) uses a HunYuan V1 language backbone (`hunyuan_v1.py: HunYuanAttention`), which builds a **standard `Attention`** (head_dim=128, num_kv_heads=8 → **gqa_ratio=2**), not `MLAAttention`. 3. **The ROCm CK custom paged-attention kernel is gated out**, so vLLM uses the Triton kernel. On gfx1100, `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention()` (`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`) requires `gqa_ratio∈[3,16]`; **gqa_ratio=2 fails**, so the CK kernel is disabled and vLLM falls back to **Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d`** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py`). The run logs confirm both: ``` WARNING [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation. WARNING [jit_monitor.py:129] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: kernel_paged_attention_2d. ... consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config. ``` Symptom A (first-call non-determinism) lines up with that kernel being JIT-compiled on first use (hence warmup eliminates it). Symptom B (long-seq corruption) lines up with that Triton kernel not matching the (correct) torch-SDPA numerics at long bf16 sequences on gfx1100. #### Ask 1. **First-call determinism (symptom A):** vLLM's own `jit_monitor` says to "extend warmup to cover this shape/config." Can engine warmup be extended to cover the paged-attention decode shape so the **first** real request is deterministic (not just the second onward)? 2. **Long-seq correctness (symptom B):** can the Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d` numerics on gfx1100 be made to match torch-SDPA at long bf16 sequences — or can the **CK custom paged kernel** be extended to `gqa_ratio=2` (and the HunYuan V1 GQA config) so RDNA3 uses the deterministic CK path instead of the Triton fallback? 3. **Scope:** gfx1100/RDNA3 is a consumer GPU. Is paged-attention determinism/correctness on RDNA3 within vLLM's ROCm support scope (which I understand to be CDNA/MI-series focused)? If RDNA3 is community-supported only, happy to move/dupe this to the right place. Happy to attach the rendered page image, raw token ids, or full run logs on request. Thanks! > Note: vLLM 0.25.1 is not a HunyuanOCR-model-card-listed vLLM version (card lists 0.18.1 / nightly / 0.13). I'm reporting because the failure looks like a platform/kernel-architecture issue (gfx1100 paged-attention), not a model-compat one.

All 32 lanes fault together, i.e. the whole tile's base pointer is bad rather than a tail element being over-read. The faulting address sits ~90 GB below the other live pointers. ### Where the int32 comes from `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flex_attention.py` builds `kv_indices` as int32 (still true on `main` as of 2026-07-30): ```python kv_indices = unique_static_unsorted((used_pages_padded.long()), M=self.num_blocks).to(torch.int32) kv_indices = copy_to_persistent(self.persistent_kv_indices, kv_indices) self.persistent_kv_indices = torch.empty( self.max_num_query_groups, self.max_num_kv_indices, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device) ``` so every downstream term stays in that dtype (`kv_start = kv_indices * block_size`, `ptr = K + offs_n * stride_kn`). The generated kernel does define `INDEX_DTYPE = tl.int64`, but only the **output store** indices go through it; the K/V gather offsets do not. What makes the offset exceed the K tensor's own `numel` is that **K and V share one buffer**, so the K view's maximum linear offset spans the *whole* buffer while its `numel` is only half of it. Inductor appears to pick the index dtype from `numel` (~1.12e9 here, which fits int32) rather than from the stride-derived maximum offset (~2.24e9, which does not). ⚠️ **The packing axis differs between releases — this needs updating before submitting.** Our environment (`0.23.1rc1.dev813+g344609ab1`) packs on a dedicated dim and splits with `unbind`: ```python # flex_attention.py:133 (dev813, what we measured) return (num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size) # flex_attention.py:1245 / :1350 key_cache, value_cache = kv_cache.unbind(1) ``` `main` (2026-07-30) packs into the content dim instead: ```python # K and V are packed into the content dim: logical (B, H, N, 2*hs). return (num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size) ... kv_cache = kv_cache.transpose(1, 2) key_cache, value_cache = kv_cache.split(hs, dim=-1) ``` The bound is **unchanged** by this, because in both layouts the buffer holds `num_blocks * block_size * (2 * num_kv_heads * head_size)` elements and the K view's maximum offset reaches the far end of it: ``` max_safe_num_gpu_blocks = 2**31 // (block_size * 2 * num_kv_heads * head_size) = 2**31 // (16 * 2 * 8 * 128) = 65,536 ``` but the *per-token* stride differs, so **the `main` derivation above is analytical — we measured the `unbind` layout, not the packed one.** Re-run snippet (b) against `main`'s layout before filing. Bisecting one property at a time on the layout we did measure, the shared buffer is the only necessary condition: replacing the two strided views with separate contiguous K/V tensors halves the stride and doubles the bound. `kv_indices` contiguity, Q layout, `enable_gqa`, `Q_LEN` alignment and `KV_LEN` magnitude are all irrelevant. Also note `kv_cache_utils.py` now has a `_use_packed_kv_cache_config` / `_get_packed_kv_cache_layout` path returning a `block_stride`; whether that changes the effective stride for this backend is **not checked**. ### Who is exposed `num_blocks = available_memory // (group_size * page_size)` where `group_size = max(len(g.layer_names) for g in kv_cache_groups)` — the number of memory pools the hybrid allocator creates. **Exposure grows as `group_size` shrinks**, so models whose layers split into many KV cache groups are the most exposed; a uniform single-group model needs proportionally more memory to reach the bound. Being upfront about our own trigger: we reached `num_gpu_blocks = 70,315` with an **out-of-tree** backend whose per-layer window config split 36 layers into 4 groups (`group_size = 9`, 37.56 GiB of KV cache). The same 36 layers as a single group give only ~17,579 blocks. So this is not straightforward to reproduce with a stock uniform model on one 80 GB card — hence snippet (b), which exercises the kernel-level mechanism directly and needs neither vLLM nor weights. In memory terms the bound is `4 GiB * group_size` of KV cache per pool group (bf16, this layout). Two-mode summary: | condition | result | | --- | --- | | block id < bound | correct | | block id ≥ bound, wrapped address unmapped | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` | | block id ≥ bound, wrapped address **mapped** | **no error — silently reads the neighbouring allocation, wrong output** | Consistent with a latent bound rather than a workload issue: everything that appeared to "fix" it — lowering `gpu_memory_utilization`, capping `max_num_seqs`, enabling eviction, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` — merely keeps the allocator from handing out block ids at the top of the pool. ### Upstream status The int32 offset arithmetic itself lives in PyTorch's generated FlexAttention kernel and **has since been fixed**: [pytorch#190857](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/190857) (closed) and [PR #185264](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/185264), which adds an `INDEX_DTYPE` parameter to `load_checked_2d` and casts the offsets before they are multiplied by strides, at every call site in the forward, backward and common templates. So on a torch that carries #185264 this should no longer be reachable, even with int32 `kv_indices`. It remains reachable on releases without it — ours (`2.11.0+cu128`) has `INDEX_DTYPE` appearing zero times in `torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/templates/utilities.py.jinja`. ### Suggested mitigations on the vLLM side 1. **Validate at start-up** (cheap, no perf impact): warn or clamp when `num_gpu_blocks` exceeds `2**31 // (block_size * kv_packing * num_kv_heads * head_size)` and the running torch lacks the fix. We do this out-of-tree by wrapping `kv_cache_utils.may_override_num_blocks`; it cost 4.1% of pool capacity (70,315 → 65,536 blocks, 243,350 → 233,263 tokens) with no measurable throughput change, and it removed both failure modes. 2. Or declare a **minimum torch version** for the FlexAttention backend. 3. Optionally, a **non-interleaved** K/V layout for this backend — halving the row stride doubles the bound regardless of the torch version. FWIW the `persistent_rswa_kv_indices` comment in the same file already documents an adjacent hazard ("... producing an out-of-bounds K/V pointer and a CUDA illegal memory access") and fixes it for the R-SWA path only; this report is the non-R-SWA path with a different mechanism. - [x] Searched existing issues (found none covering the int32 index bound; #13824 / #23814 / #33242 / #35706 / #39025 are unrelated illegal-memory-access reports)

items.title: [CI] Detect and fail evals on when NaNs appear in logits
items.body:
This PR sets `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` in several evals so we can test against NaNs. 

NaNs appearing in logits often co-appear with KV cache NaNs, which is a catastrophic failure mode for a inference service since attention kernels mask with multiplication by zero. (see https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/1974)

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex

items.title: [Core] Add --enable-nan-fault-tolerance for NaN detection and request abort
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds `--enable-detect-nans-in-logits` CLI flag (replaces `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` env var with a proper engine arg, keeps env var for backward compat)
- Adds `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance` CLI flag which implies `--enable-detect-nans-in-logits` and additionally:
  - **Aborts requests** when NaN values are detected in logits — during chunked prefill intermediate chunks, final chunks, or decode steps
  - **Forces KV cache block zeroing** on reuse (`needs_kv_cache_zeroing` returns `True`) to prevent stale NaN data from being read by subsequent requests
  - **Evicts the aborted request's blocks from the prefix cache** so a NaN-corrupted block that prefill committed to the cache cannot be matched (and read) as a prefix-cache hit by a later request with the same prefix

## Motivation

Currently, `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` only flags corrupted requests as a Prometheus metric (`vllm:corrupted_requests`). The request continues running to completion, meaning:

- Corrupted KV cache blocks can be reused via prefix caching
- NaN KV data gets offloaded to CPU/disk tiers
- In disaggregated PD, corrupted KV is transferred per-layer to decode instances via NIXL before the NaN is even detected in logits

This PR adds a fault-tolerance mode that aborts requests on NaN detection and zeroes freed blocks on reallocation, preventing corruption from propagating.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/observability.py` — two new fields + model validator for implication
- `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` — wire flags through to `ObservabilityConfig`
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py` — accept `detect_nans_in_logits` at init instead of reading the env var directly
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` — pass `detect_nans_in_logits` from `ObservabilityConfig` into the **V2 model runner's** `Sampler`. This is the default runner; without this the flag had no effect there (the sampler defaulted to `compute_nans=False`, so `num_nans` was never computed and `num_nans_in_logits` was never populated on the model runner output). The async output path (`gpu/async_utils.py`) already forwards `num_nans` to `ModelRunnerOutput`.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` — check config flag alongside env var for NaN detection (legacy V1 runner)
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — abort requests with NaN logits via existing `finish_requests(FINISHED_ERROR)` path; **also evict the aborted request's blocks from the prefix cache** (`kv_cache_manager.evict_blocks`) before freeing them. Prefill commits full blocks to the prefix cache at schedule time (before the forward writes KV), so a block holding NaN KV would otherwise stay matchable and be reused as a prefix-cache hit by a later request (hits are never re-zeroed). Eviction also resets the block hash, so `free()` prioritizes those blocks for reallocation, where the zero-on-allocation path wipes them. This mirrors the existing KV-load-failure recovery path.
- `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py` — `force_zeroing` field on `KVCacheConfig`, checked in `needs_kv_cache_zeroing`
- `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` — set `force_zeroing` from `enable_nan_fault_tolerance` at `KVCacheConfig` construction
- `vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py` — remove redundant `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` gate on `is_corrupted` (NaN count is only non-zero when detection is enabled)

## Known Limitations

- NIXL transfers KV per-layer during the forward pass (`save_kv_layer`). By the time NaN is detected in logits (post-forward), the current step's KV may already be on the decode instance. The abort prevents future steps but cannot recall already-transferred data.
- The KV cache for the chunk that produced NaN is already written. Abort evicts those blocks from the prefix cache (so they can't be matched as a hit) and zeroing wipes them on reallocation.
- Detection is on logits. If a NaN corrupts the KV of a *decode* step, that step's token is not committed to the prefix cache before the abort frees the request, so decode-phase NaN blocks never become matchable. The prefix-cache exposure is specific to prefill, where full blocks are committed at schedule time — which is exactly what the eviction closes.

## End-to-end testing guide

Verified on the default (V2) GPU model runner with **async scheduling** using `Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B`. A healthy model rarely emits NaN logits on demand, so both tests use a one-line debug edit to force a NaN, then observe the two behaviors the flag controls: (A) the request is **aborted**, and (B) the freed KV blocks are **zeroed on reuse**.

### Part A — NaN in logits aborts the request

**1. Force a NaN.** In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py`, inside `Sampler.__call__`, add one line immediately before:

```python
        num_nans = get_num_nans(logits) if self.compute_nans else None
```

so it reads:

```python
        logits[-1, 0] = float("nan")  # debug: force a NaN
        num_nans = get_num_nans(logits) if self.compute_nans else None
```

**2. Start the server** (async scheduling on):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B \
    --enable-nan-fault-tolerance \
    --async-scheduling \
    --max-model-len 2048
```

The startup config confirms the implication: `enable_detect_nans_in_logits=True, enable_nan_fault_tolerance=True`.

**3. Send a request:**

```bash
curl -s -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":20,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected — the request is aborted instead of returning a (corrupt) completion:

```
HTTP=500
# engine log:
WARNING [scheduler.py] Request <id> aborted: 1 NaN values in logits
```

**Control:** restart the same server **without** `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance` (keeping the debug line). The identical request now returns `HTTP=200` with a normal completion — the NaN is counted in the metric but the request is not aborted.

### Part B — freed KV blocks are zeroed on reuse

The flag also makes `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` return `True`, so every block is zeroed when it is (re)allocated to a request — the block a NaN-aborted request wrote is wiped before another request can reuse it. It does **not** zero the whole KV cache (that would be prohibitively expensive); it zeroes exactly the blocks each request touches, at allocation time.

**1. Observe the zeroing.** In `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`, add a print at the top of `KVBlockZeroer.zero_block_ids`:

```python
    def zero_block_ids(self, block_ids: list[int]) -> None:
        """Zero the KV cache memory for the given block IDs."""
        print(f"[kv-zero] zeroing {len(block_ids)} block(s): {block_ids[:8]}", flush=True)  # debug
        if not block_ids or self._meta is None:
            return
```

**2. Serve with the flag** (keep the Part A NaN injection so requests abort and free their blocks):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B --enable-nan-fault-tolerance --async-scheduling --max-model-len 2048
```

**3. Send a short and a long prompt:**

```bash
# short prompt (fits in one 16-token block)
curl -s -o /dev/null http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":20,"temperature":0}'

# long prompt (spans several blocks)
curl -s -o /dev/null http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B","prompt":"Please summarize in great detail the following passage and then continue the narrative: once upon a time in a distant kingdom by the sea there lived a wise old scholar who studied the stars and the tides","max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected — the number of zeroed blocks scales with each request's block footprint (block 0 is the reserved null block, so allocation starts at block 1). Each aborted request frees its blocks, and the next request re-zeroes them on reallocation:

```
[kv-zero] zeroing 1 block(s): [1]              # short prompt
[kv-zero] zeroing 4 block(s): [1, 2, 3, 4]     # long prompt
```

**Control:** restart **without** `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance`. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` is `False`, so `[kv-zero]` never prints — no blocks are zeroed and requests complete normally.

### Part C — an aborted request's blocks are evicted from the prefix cache

This is the correctness case the eviction closes: prefill commits a full block to the prefix cache **at schedule time, before the forward writes KV**. If that forward produces NaN, the block is already matchable. The abort must evict it, or a later request with the same prefix would reuse the NaN KV as a cache hit (hits are never re-zeroed).

To make the NaN fire on a *real* request (not warmup, which also runs the sampler), arm it from a file instead of the always-on line in Part A. In `Sampler.__call__`, immediately before the `num_nans = ...` line:

```python
        import os as _dbg_os
        if _dbg_os.path.exists("/tmp/arm_nan"):
            _dbg_os.remove("/tmp/arm_nan")
            logits[-1, 0] = float("nan")  # debug: one real-request NaN
```

Add a log line at the top of `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` to observe prefix-cache reuse, and one in `BlockPool.evict_blocks`:

```python
# get_computed_blocks, right before `return blocks, num_new_computed_tokens, ...`
        print(f"[prefix-hit] req={request.request_id} new_computed_tokens={num_new_computed_tokens}", flush=True)
# evict_blocks, first line
        print(f"[evict] block_ids={sorted(block_ids)}", flush=True)
```

Serve with the flag, then send the **same** prompt twice — the first arms and aborts, the second reuses (or, with the fix, does not):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B --enable-nan-fault-tolerance --async-scheduling --max-model-len 2048

P="The capital of France is Paris and the capital of Germany is Berlin and the capital of Italy is Rome and the capital of Spain is"
touch /tmp/arm_nan
curl -s -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B\",\"prompt\":\"$P\",\"max_tokens\":10,\"temperature\":0}"   # request #1
curl -s -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B\",\"prompt\":\"$P\",\"max_tokens\":10,\"temperature\":0}"   # request #2
```

Expected — request #1 aborts (`HTTP=500`), its blocks are evicted, and request #2 gets **no** prefix-cache reuse of the NaN block:

```
[dbg-nan] ...                         # on request #1's forward
WARNING [scheduler.py] Request <id-1> aborted: 1 NaN values in logits
[evict] block_ids=[1, 2]              # NaN block(s) evicted from the prefix cache
[prefix-hit] req=<id-2> new_computed_tokens=0   # request #2 recomputes; does NOT reuse the NaN block
HTTP=200                              # request #2 completes cleanly
```

**Control:** temporarily disable the eviction (`if False and nan_block_ids:`). `[evict]` no longer prints and request #2 shows `new_computed_tokens=16` — it matches and reuses the block request #1 wrote during the NaN step. That reuse is exactly what the eviction prevents.

## Test plan

- [x] `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance` implies `--enable-detect-nans-in-logits` (confirmed in startup config)
- [x] NaN in logits aborts the request (`FINISHED_ERROR` → `HTTP 500`) on the default V2 runner, with `--async-scheduling`
- [x] Without the flag, a NaN-producing request completes normally (control)
- [x] Freed KV blocks are zeroed on reuse when the flag is enabled; not zeroed without it (control)
- [x] An aborted request's blocks are evicted from the prefix cache — a later same-prefix request does not reuse the NaN block (`new_computed_tokens=0` with the fix vs `16` without)
- [ ] Verify abort works during intermediate chunked prefill (discarded logits still trigger abort)
- [ ] Verify existing `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` env var still works (backward compat)
- [ ] Run existing scheduler and model runner tests for regressions

items.title: [Kernel] Harden top_k_per_row against NaN and under-filled output
items.body:
## Purpose

Addresses the kernel-hardening portion of #49896: prevent `top_k_per_row_prefill` (and the shared `topKPerRowJob` used by the decode/split variants) from emitting uninitialized or invalid indices when NaN values leave fewer than `top_k` selectable candidates.

Root cause in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`: `extractBinIdx` bins positive-NaN bit patterns above +inf, so NaN-dominated rows place the histogram threshold bin on a NaN bin; the insertion-sort final pass's NaN comparisons all evaluate false, so every threshold-bin element writes slot 0 and the remaining `smemOutput` slots keep uninitialized dynamic shared memory, which the unconditional final store loop emits as indices. With fewer than `top_k` non-NaN candidates, `smemThresholdBinIdx` is additionally read unset. Downstream gathers with the garbage indices then hit device-side asserts / illegal memory access.

Changes (kernel `+42/−1`, tests `+209`):
- `isNaNLogit()` bit-pattern test (robust under `--use_fast_math`, HIP-compatible via `__float_as_uint`);
- NaN exclusion in both `distributeToBins` and `processBins`, kept consistent so histogram counts match prefix sums;
- well-defined fallback when fewer than `top_k` candidates exist (`smemThresholdBinIdx = kNumBins`, `smemFinalBinSize = 0`);
- `smemOutput` pre-filled with `-1` (multi-block variant also `-FLT_MAX` logit halves), `finalIndices[ii] = -1` init in the radix path, and a `-1`-preserving rebase in the strided final store — under-filled rows now return `-1` padding like the short-row path instead of garbage.

Scope notes:
- This does not change DeepSeek-V4 routing (#49897 territory), the upstream NaN source (DeepGEMM side), or the downstream gather.
- The short-row path (`rowLen <= topK`) keeps its documented "return all candidate positions" behavior (memory-safe); #49897's torch fallback excludes NaN even for short rows — deliberate, called out for reviewers.

## Test Plan

Hardware: H200 / SM90 (driver 580.65.06), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc 13.0.48), torch 2.13.0+cu130, kernel built from source (`_C_stable_libtorch`) for both parent and patched in the same job/toolchain, on top of current main (`7f4c52f2`). The defect is data-driven (NaN input), per the issue not SM120-specific — confirmed: the unmodified kernel fails identically on H200.

- Canary: the issue's reproduction (clean vs 83%-NaN logits; output prefilled with `-7`, checking garbage / unwritten / out-of-range / NaN-selected rows).
- New tests in `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`: 16 NaN cases covering prefill insertion-sort and radix-sort variants (4869-row and 12544-row shapes) and decode insertion / radix / split+merge (8192 / 16384 / 250000), NaN fractions 0.5 / 0.83 / 1.0, asserting: all indices in `[-1, rowLen)`, no unwritten sentinel survives, exactly `min(top_k, num_finite)` valid indices with `-1` suffix padding, and selected values equal to a NaN-excluded `torch.topk` reference.
- Regression: full existing `test_top_k_per_row.py`.
- `compute-sanitizer` memcheck on the canary + prefill NaN + decode NaN cases, and initcheck on the canary (patched build).

## Test Result

| Input | Parent (unpatched) | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| clean finite | 166 passed / 6 skipped (reference set-equality) | 166 passed / 6 skipped — unchanged |
| partial NaN, finite ≥ k | NaN tests FAILED (wrong/garbage sets) | 16 passed — finite-only top-k equals reference |
| partial NaN, finite < k | canary: device-side assert (`AcceleratorError`); NaN tests FAILED | canary PASS (`garbage_rows=0 unwritten_rows=0 nan_selected_hist_rows=0 out_of_range_rows=0`); tests assert finite indices + `-1` padding |
| all NaN | NaN tests FAILED (garbage/NaN-bit indices) | 16 passed — all `-1` on histogram rows |

- New NaN tests: parent 16 failed → patched 16 passed (identical test code, same job).
- `compute-sanitizer`: memcheck ×3 and initcheck ×1 all `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`.
- Reverse A/B on the pre-rebase tree: unpatched `.so` swapped back → 16 failed; patched restored → canary PASS.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix NaN handling in rejection sampler tl.argmax
items.body:
## Summary

`tl.argmax` on an all-NaN block returns an out-of-range block index (pointing into the padded region beyond `num_blocks - 1`). That index is used to load from the local-argmax tensor, producing an out-of-bounds read and an illegal memory access downstream in the rejection sampler.

Two kernels in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` are affected:

- `_compute_global_target_argmax` — `tl.argmax(local_max)` at line 111, result used to index `target_local_argmax_ptr` at line 113.
- `_insert_resampled_kernel` — `tl.argmax(resampled_local_max)` at line 852, result used to index `resampled_local_argmax_ptr` at line 854.

When all values in the (padded) block dimension are NaN — reachable via NaN target logits — `tl.argmax` does not guarantee an in-range result. The loaded garbage index then propagates into subsequent gathers/stores, surfacing as an illegal memory access.

**Fix:** in both kernels, map NaN to `-inf` via `tl.where` before `tl.argmax`, and clamp the resulting block index to `num_blocks - 1` with `tl.minimum` as a defensive bound. Two small, surgical changes; no behavior change for non-NaN inputs.

## Symptom / reproduction

Observed as an illegal memory access during speculative-decoding warmup (DSpark) when serving Kimi-K3 on 8xB300 with TP=8. Confirmed the root cause with a standalone Triton repro on an RTX 4090:

```python
import torch, triton, triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def k(out_ptr, NUM_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr, PAD: tl.constexpr):
    blocks = tl.arange(0, PAD)
    vals = tl.full((PAD,), float("nan"), tl.float32)
    vals = tl.where(blocks < NUM_BLOCKS, vals, float("-inf"))
    idx = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0)
    tl.store(out_ptr, idx)

out = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
k[(1,)](out, NUM_BLOCKS=4, PAD=8)
print(out.item())  # unpatched: 8 (out of range); with NaN->-inf + clamp: in [0, 3]
```

On the all-NaN input, unpatched `tl.argmax` returns `idx == num_blocks` (out of range); with the NaN→-inf mapping plus clamp the index stays in range.

## Validation

- Standalone Triton repro (RTX 4090): patched kernel returns an in-range index on all-NaN input; unpatched does not.
- Full vLLM server on 8xB300, TP=8, Kimi-K3 with DSpark speculative decoding: server boots through warmup (previously IMA), generates coherent output, acceptance length 2.5, conc=1 throughput 110–116 tok/s (+58% vs no-spec).

## Disclosure

- AI assistance (Kimi K3) was used in developing this fix. A human engineer (Gabriel Peracio, Parasail) reviewed every changed line and validated the fix on hardware as described above.
- Checked for duplicates before opening: no open PR or issue covers `tl.argmax`/NaN out-of-bounds in the rejection sampler (`rejection_sampler_utils.py`).

items.title: [Core] Zero KV cache when NaN logits detected
items.body:
When `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` and NaN values are detected in logits, abort all in-flight requests, zero all KV cache blocks, and reset the prefix cache. Covers both MRV1 and MRV2 model runners.

**Limitation:** GPU-side KV cache zeroing only runs on the rank that computes logits (driver / last PP rank). Other TP/PP ranks are not explicitly zeroed. This is safe because aborted requests free all blocks, and fresh allocations go through `new_block_ids_to_zero` which zeros on all ranks — but the cleanup is implicit, not explicit.

Model: `meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct` (chunked local attention / iRoPE, `attention_chunk_size=8192`), FlashInfer V1 backend, TP=8. Originally observed on GB10/sm121 (DGX Spark, where FlashInfer is the auto-default); reproduced here on H100/sm90 by forcing `--attention-backend FLASHINFER`. The defect is also present on current `main` by source inspection.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Serving a Llama-4 model (chunked local attention, `attention_chunk_size=8192`) with the FlashInfer V1 attention backend crashes during attention-metadata construction whenever a request's prefill length exceeds `attention_chunk_size` **and** `--max-num-seqs` is small (e.g. 1), with `ValueError: provided out is the wrong size for the accumulation`.

**Root cause (traced through source).** `make_local_attention_virtual_batches(...)` (`v1/attention/backends/utils.py`) sets `num_reqs = cu_num_blocks[-1]`, inflating it to the virtual-batch count (`local_blocks = 1 + cdiv(q_seqlen - q_tokens_in_first_block, attn_chunk_size)` per request). `ChunkedLocalAttentionBuilder.build()` passes this inflated metadata to the FlashInfer builder, which preallocates `paged_kv_indptr = _make_buffer(max_num_seqs + 1)`, `paged_kv_last_page_len = _make_buffer(max_num_seqs)`, `paged_kv_indices = _make_buffer(max_num_seqs * max_num_pages_per_req)`. In `_compute_flashinfer_kv_metadata(...)`, `np.cumsum(num_blocks_np, dtype=np.int32, out=self.paged_kv_indptr.np[1 : num_reqs + 1])` overflows the `max_num_seqs+1`-sized buffer.

**Minimal reproduction.**

```bash
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --max-model-len 36000 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --enable-prefix-caching
# --load-format dummy can skip weight download; the crash is weight-independent.
```

Send a completion request with input longer than `attention_chunk_size` (~34000 tokens). On Hopper the backend must be forced with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER` (FA3 is otherwise auto-selected and does not hit this path); on Blackwell/SM12.x FlashInfer is the auto-default.

**Redacted traceback.**

```
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4321, in execute_model
  File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line 1281, in build
    paged_kv_indices = self._compute_flashinfer_kv_metadata(
  File ".../vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line 1076, in _compute_flashinfer_kv_metadata
    np.cumsum(num_blocks_np, dtype=np.int32, out=self.paged_kv_indptr.np[1 : num_reqs + 1])
  File ".../numpy/_core/fromnumeric.py", line 2955, in cumsum
    return _wrapfunc(a, 'cumsum', axis=axis, dtype=dtype, out=out)
ValueError: provided out is the wrong size for the accumulation.
```

(`CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is not supported with ChunkedLocalAttention_..._FlashInferBackend ... setting cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` — so the failing prefill path is not under fixed-address CUDA-graph constraints.)

**Expected behavior.** Serving a documented Llama-4 long-context configuration should not crash. The FlashInfer builder should size `paged_kv_indptr` / `paged_kv_last_page_len` / `paged_kv_indices` for the maximum virtual-batch count chunked local attention can produce (a function of `max_model_len`, `attention_chunk_size`, `block_size`), or reallocate when `num_reqs` exceeds the preallocated capacity — rather than sizing solely by `max_num_seqs`.

**Validated fix.** Growing the three buffers on overflow resolves the crash and the previously-crashing configuration then serves inference successfully (5/5 requests, 0 errors) on the same public nightly image. `cudagraph_mode` is PIECEWISE on this path, so reallocation is safe. Effective patch:

```python
# before np.cumsum(..., out=self.paged_kv_indptr.np[1:num_reqs+1])
if num_reqs + 1 > self.paged_kv_indptr.np.shape[0]:
    self.paged_kv_indptr = self._make_buffer(num_reqs + 1)
    self.paged_kv_indptr_cpu_buffer = torch.zeros_like(
        self.paged_kv_indptr.cpu, pin_memory=self.pin_memory
    )
if num_reqs > self.paged_kv_last_page_len.np.shape[0]:
    self.paged_kv_last_page_len = self._make_buffer(num_reqs)

# after num_actual_pages = self.paged_kv_indptr.np[num_reqs]
if int(num_actual_pages) > self.paged_kv_indices.np.shape[0]:
    self.paged_kv_indices = self._make_buffer(int(num_actual_pages))
```

items.title: [Bugfix] Route DSv4 sparse-indexer prefill top-k around NaN-broken kernel path on SM12x
items.body:
FIX #49896 (the crash layer; the NaN-logits layer of that issue remains open).

## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM12x (enabled by #43477) crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access on the first prefill longer than ~2048 tokens. Root cause chain (full tensor-level evidence in #49896):

1. `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` emits NaN-dominated logits on SM12x (83→100% NaN cascade).
2. `top_k_per_row_prefill`'s histogram path (rows with more candidates than `top_k`) mishandles NaN input: it writes NaN bit patterns (`0x7FC00000` = 2143289344) as candidate indices and leaves part of its dynamic-smem output unwritten, copying uninitialized memory out as indices. Reproducible in a 25-line standalone script (see the issue); with clean input the kernel is correct on SM120 (upstream unit test passes 12/12 here).
3. `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens` trusts `local_idx >= 0` and gathers `block_table[req, INT32_MAX // block_size]` → IMA on all TP ranks.

This PR routes SM12x prefill top-k through a `torch.topk` implementation of the kernel's documented contract: top-k of `logits[i, ks_i:ke_i)` relative to `ks_i`, ascending position order, `-1` padding for short rows, NaN never selected. It mirrors the decode path, which already excludes SM12x from `cooperative_topk`.

Deliberately narrow:
- **Not** a csrc change: the kernel's NaN mishandling is data-driven and deserves hardening for every arch (never emit unwritten smem; exclude NaN), but we cannot build/test csrc on the affected hardware — left to the issue.
- **Not** a fix for the NaN logits themselves (the primary SM12x defect; cf. the e8m0→fp32 upcast and SM120 DeepGEMM fallbacks in #41834). With NaN scores, any correct top-k selects an arbitrary candidate set, so SM12x DSv4 output quality for long prompts remains degraded until that lands. This PR converts a hard engine crash into defined, contract-correct behavior and is a prerequisite for any further SM12x DSv4 work.

## Test Plan

- New contract test `test_top_k_per_row_prefill_torch_fallback` (runs on any CUDA device): set-equality with the `torch.topk` reference per row, ascending order, in-range, `-1` padding, NaN exclusion.
- Real-workload validation on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (SM120, TP=4), vLLM 0.26.0 + flashinfer 0.6.14, DeepSeek-V4-Flash: the previously 9×-reproducible crash (16 concurrent structured-output requests, mixed 0.5–8K-token prefill) is eliminated — zero illegal memory accesses, zero garbage indices in the consumer across repeated full fan-outs; engine survives and serves.

## Test Result

- `test_top_k_per_row_prefill_torch_fallback`: 6/6 pass on SM120.
- Existing `test_top_k_per_row` (CUDA kernel, clean inputs): 12/12 pass on SM120, unaffected by this change.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 on SM12x: NaN MQA logits drive top_k_per_row_prefill to emit uninitialized smem as indices -> illegal memory access
items.body:
### Environment

- vLLM 0.26.0 (release wheel), flashinfer-python 0.6.14, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.126.09
- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (SM120), TP=4
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code`, OpenAI-compatible server

### Symptom

DeepSeek-V4-Flash on SM120 (enabled by #43477) crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` on all TP ranks → `EngineDeadError`, on the first prefill batch containing a request longer than ~2048 tokens (e.g. 16 concurrent structured-output requests with 0.5–8K-token prompts; also a single ~5K-token prompt). Short prompts serve perfectly. We reproduced the crash 9 times across vLLM 0.25.1/0.26.0 and flashinfer 0.6.13/0.6.14/0.6.15.

Under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the fault is raised in the Triton kernel `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py`), reached from `DeepseekV4FlashInferSM120Attention._forward_prefill` (compress-ratio-4 branch).

### Root-cause chain (instrumented at the tensor level)

**1. `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` produces NaN-dominated logits on SM120.**
Auditing the valid `[ks, ke)` region of the prefill MQA logits per C4A layer on a single 4,972-token prefill: the first C4A layer is **83% NaN** (2,560,388 of 3,088,855 entries; the finite remainder looks plausible, range ≈ −2…4), and every subsequent layer is **100% NaN** (cascade through the model). This is presumably the SM12x scale-handling issue (cf. the e8m0→fp32 upcast in #41834).

**2. `top_k_per_row_prefill` mishandles NaN input on its histogram path and emits uninitialized shared memory as indices.**
Auditing `topk_indices_buffer` immediately after `ops.top_k_per_row_prefill` returns: rows whose candidate count `rowLen = ke−ks ≤ topk` (the short-row path) are clean (`-1`-padded as documented); rows with `rowLen > topk` (histogram path) contain garbage starting at exactly the first such row, e.g. rows 2051…4868 of a 4,869-token request at compress ratio 4 (2051/4 ≈ 513 > 512 = `index_topk`). Garbage row counts differ across TP ranks on identical input (1923/2151/2120/1987) — nondeterministic, consistent with uninitialized dynamic shared memory (`smemOutput` is never pre-initialized and the final copy loop writes all `topK` slots).

This reproduces **in isolation, without serving** (25 lines, below): with clean random logits the kernel is correct on SM120 (0 garbage rows, and `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` passes 12/12 here); with 83%-NaN logits, ~40% of histogram-path rows contain garbage. Two distinct failure signatures:
- indices equal to `2143289344 = 0x7FC00000` — a **float32 NaN bit pattern reinterpreted as an int32 index**;
- output slots that keep their pre-launch canary value — i.e. **never written at all** (in serving these become whatever is in shared memory).

Since the repro is data-driven (NaN input) rather than SM120-specific, the kernel's NaN mishandling likely affects all architectures; SM120 is where NaN logits actually occur in practice.

```python
import torch, vllm  # importing vllm registers the _C ops
torch.manual_seed(0); torch.set_default_device("cuda:0")

rows, cols, top_k = 4869, 1243, 512
ks = torch.zeros(rows, dtype=torch.int32)
ke = torch.clamp(torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int32) // 4 + 1, max=cols)

def probe(tag, logits):
    out = torch.full((rows, top_k), -7, dtype=torch.int32)  # -7 = canary
    torch.ops._C.top_k_per_row_prefill(logits, ks, ke, out, rows,
                                       logits.stride(0), logits.stride(1), top_k)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    garb = (out >= 1_000_000) | ((out < -1) & (out != -7))
    print(f"{tag}: garbage_rows={int(garb.any(dim=1).sum())}/{rows} "
          f"unwritten_rows={int((out == -7).any(dim=1).sum())} max={int(out.max())}")

logits = torch.randn(rows, cols)
probe("clean ", logits.clone())                                  # 0 garbage
nanl = logits.clone(); nanl[torch.rand(rows, cols) < 0.83] = float("nan")
probe("83%NaN", nanl)   # ~1800 garbage rows, ~500 unwritten, max=2143289344
```

**3. `compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens` dereferences the garbage.**
Its validity mask is only `local_idx >= 0`, so `INT32_MAX`-class indices pass and it gathers `block_table[req, idx // block_size]` far out of bounds → the illegal memory access that kills the engine.

### Behavioral confirmation

Needle-in-haystack on the same server: a prompt below the sparse threshold retrieves the needle perfectly ("The secret code word is BLUEBERRY."); the identical needle in a ~4.5K-token prompt yields output completely unrelated to the prompt (the model hallucinates arbitrary code/text — its selected KV set is effectively random). Short prompts mask defect (1) entirely because when `rowLen ≤ topk` the top-k selects *all* candidates and scores never matter.

### Suggested fixes (layered)

1. **Kernel hardening (`csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`)**: the histogram path should never emit unwritten smem or NaN bit patterns as indices — pad under-filled output with `-1` like the short-row path, and exclude NaN scores from selection. Data-driven robustness fix, valuable on every arch. (We can't build csrc locally to contribute this ourselves.)
2. **SM12x routing**: until (1) lands, route SM12x prefill top-k through a `torch.topk` implementation of the kernel's documented contract — the decode path already excludes SM12x from `cooperative_topk`. PR incoming; verified on the affected hardware that the previously 9×-reproducible crash is eliminated.

items.title: [Bugfix] Skip linear bias in layerwise reload to avoid corruption

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

Linear layers that carry a `bias` are corrupted when loaded through the online quantization + layerwise-reload path (e.g. online FP8). After loading, `bias` holds uninitialized memory instead of the checkpoint values.

**Root cause.** The linear base class creates `bias` *after* `create_weights()`. Online quantization calls `initialize_online_processing()` from inside `create_weights()`, i.e. before `bias` exists, so:

1. `load_numel_total = get_layer_size(layer)` counts only `weight`, and
2. `bias`'s weight loader is never wrapped into `online_process_loader`, so it is never buffered into `info.loaded_weights`.

As soon as `weight` finishes loading, `load_numel >= load_numel_total` holds and `_layerwise_process()` runs. `materialize_layer()` re-allocates every non-skipped tensor of the layer via `empty_strided` — including the already-loaded, non-meta `bias` — replacing its real values with uninitialized memory. Since `bias` is absent from `loaded_weights`, the replay loop never writes it back, so the corruption is permanent.

**Fix.** Add `"bias"` to `SKIP_TENSORS`. `bias` is never quantized (FP8 only quantizes `weight`; `bias` stays bf16 and is added after the GEMM), it is tiny, and it is eager-loaded on the normal path, so it should never be moved to meta or re-materialized by the layerwise-reload path.

## Test Plan

Load a model with biased linear layers (Qwen3 vision tower `visual.blocks.*` qkv/proj/mlp) using online FP8 quantization + layerwise reload, then compare every `bias` parameter against the original bf16 checkpoint with `torch.allclose`.

## Test Result

- **Before:** all 110 vision-tower biases mismatch the checkpoint (`allclose` fails; values are uninitialized/zero).
- **After:** all 110 biases match the checkpoint exactly (`allclose` passes).

Tracing on `visual.blocks.0.attn.proj` confirms the mechanism: `load_numel_total=1327104` (weight only) while the recomputed layer size at trigger time is `1328256` — the 1152-element difference is exactly the bias (hidden dim). Before the fix the bias pointer changes and `absmax` drops from 3.578 to 0 across `materialize_layer()`; after the fix the pointer is unchanged and the values are preserved.

### Describe the bug Bug ---------- MRotaryEmbedding Triton kernel hardcodes Neox-style rotation, producing wrong results for GPT-J style models. Background ---------- MRotaryEmbedding is the multi-dimensional rotary position encoding operator used by vision-language models (e.g. Qwen2-VL, GLM-OCR). It extends standard RoPE by assigning separate position indices to temporal (T), height (H), and width (W) dimensions, enabling a single transformer to encode both text sequences and spatial image patches. Two rotation pairing conventions exist: - Neox style: pair (x[i], x[i + rotary_dim/2]) — half-split - GPT-J style: pair (x[2j], x[2j+1]) — interleaved even/odd The base class ``MRotaryEmbedding`` exposes an ``is_neox_style`` flag so that downstream kernels can select the correct pairing. Problem ------- The Triton kernel ``_triton_mrope_forward``, which is the CUDA/NPU fast-path invoked from ``forward_cuda``, hardcodes Neox-style rotation pairing and completely ignores the ``is_neox_style`` flag. When a model that requires GPT-J style rotation (e.g. GLM-4V, GLM-OCR) runs through this path, every rotary-dimension element is paired with its wrong counterpart: Expected (GPT-J): rotate(x[0], x[1]), rotate(x[2], x[3]), ... Actual (Neox): rotate(x[0], x[64]), rotate(x[1], x[65]), ... ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ incorrect pairing This silently corrupts all positional encodings. The model still runs to completion but produces garbled / nonsensical output — a failure mode that is hard to diagnose because no error is raised. Root Cause ---------- The Triton kernel ``_triton_mrope_forward`` has no parameter for rotation style; the even/odd offset calculation for GPT-J is simply missing. Bug Reproduction ------------ 1. End-to-end: The bug can also be verified with a real GPT-J style model such as GLM-OCR (https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-OCR): a) Default eager mode (forward_cuda invoked): ```bash $ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager ``` With image input, the model produces garbled / nonsensical output. b) Force forward_native via compilation config : ```bash $ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager --compilation-config '{"custom_ops":["all","-rotary_embedding"]}' ``` With image input, the model produces correct output. The only difference between (a) and (b) is that (b) forces vLLM to fall back to the pure PyTorch ``forward_native`` path which correctly handles GPT-J pairing. The tricky aspect of this Triton kernel bug is that it manifests when `MRotaryEmbedding` executes via the `forward_cuda` path. However, in most production deployments, models are typically served using a compiled graph mode rather than eager mode. When the model is compiled, `MRotaryEmbedding` usually defaults to the `forward_native` path, which—by coincidence—bypasses the bug. As a result, this issue often goes undetected in real-world scenarios. For example, launching the model with the default settings (i.e., without forcing eager mode) avoids the bug and functions correctly, as demonstrated in the following command: ```bash $ CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --trust-remote-code ``` It explains why the bug remains hidden under standard deployment practices.
